title: Plugin marketplace version & update verification
description:
The plugin version is pinned at `0.1.0` in both `plugins/claude-code/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (line 3) and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (top-level line 8 + `plugins[0].version` line 14). Per Claude Code docs, setting `version` pins the plugin so users only receive updates when it changes; if omitted, the version derives from the git commit SHA and `/plugin marketplace update` re-syncs automatically. The plugin files have changed since `0.1.0` was set (`skills/planner/SKILL.md` 5 commits, `hooks/hooks.json` 2 commits) but the version was never bumped — `git log` shows the version line was only ever written once in the initial F001 commit.

An Anthropic bug report (anthropics/claude-code#79950) confirms that with an unchanged pinned version, `/plugin marketplace update` reports "already at the latest version" and does NOT refresh the plugin cache, even though real content changed. The only way to force a refresh is a full uninstall + reinstall.

Open question from the 2026-08-19 investigation: the user's "old version" symptom was the MCP server version (fixed by reinstalling the global `agent-plan` npm package → 0.2.20, independent of the pin), and they ran `/plugin marketplace update` (not a plugin reinstall). It is unverified whether their Claude Code version actually refreshed the changed plugin files despite the pin, or whether the plugin files are silently stale vs `main`.

Goal: empirically verify the pin's real effect in the user's Claude Code version, then decide between (a) removing the `version` pin so updates flow automatically, or (b) keeping the pin and making `scripts/release-next.cjs` bump it (today it does not — only `scripts/release.cjs` writes the version, and it appears never run for a release, leaving the pin stale at 0.1.0).

Note: the MCP server version is independent of this — it is controlled by the global `agent-plan` CLI (`npx agent-plan mcp`) or the plugin's `npx -y @agent-plan/mcp`, not by the plugin `version` field.

Decision deferred to this phase; no code change was made as of 2026-08-19 (user chose to leave the code as-is and track the investigation here).

tasks.title: Update README and docs to reflect chosen plugin-update mechanism
tasks.description:
Update documentation to match the version strategy chosen in the sibling decision task. 

If unpinned (Option A): revise README.md — the "Update" section (around line 120) currently claims "The plugin version is bumped by `pnpm release`", and line 130 says "The release script bumps the plugin version … so `/plugin marketplace update` detects the new version"; replace with the correct behavior (plugin unpinned, version derived from git SHA, updates flow automatically on `/plugin marketplace update`). Also fix the release-notes section (around lines 1039-1041) that states the marketplace version is not bumped by `release:next` and advances on stable release — that becomes moot. 

If pinned (Option B): clarify that both `release.cjs` and `release-next.cjs` bump it. 

Ensure `docs/setup-claude-code.md` stays consistent if it references the plugin version. Keep the MCP auto-update note accurate in either case: `.mcp.json` runs `npx -y @agent-plan/mcp`, which fetches the latest published `@agent-plan/mcp` from npm, independent of the plugin `version` field.

tasks.title: Decide and implement plugin version strategy (unpin vs bump)
tasks.description:
Decide and implement the plugin version strategy based on the verification in the sibling task. 

Option A (recommended — matches the 2026-08-19 investigation conclusion that the pin is the footgun): remove the `version` pin so the plugin version derives from the git commit SHA and `/plugin marketplace update` re-syncs automatically. Implementation: delete `version` from `plugins/claude-code/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and both occurrences in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, and neutralize the plugin-version writing in `scripts/release.cjs` (the `PLUGIN_FILES` const, `readPluginVersion`/`writePluginVersion`, the `pluginTarget` computation + downgrade guard, the `writePluginVersion(pluginTarget)` call, and the commit-message line) so a stable `pnpm release` does not re-add the pin. Keep all npm package version bumping intact.

Option B: keep the pin and port the version-bump logic from `scripts/release.cjs` into `scripts/release-next.cjs` so prereleases also advance it (today `release-next.cjs` never touches it, which is why it is stuck at 0.1.0). 

Resolve the latent 0.1.0 staleness either way. Note: the MCP server launch (`npx -y @agent-plan/mcp`) is independent of this decision and must not change.

tasks.title: Verify plugin version-pin effect on marketplace update
tasks.description:
Empirically verify whether the pinned `version: 0.1.0` in `plugins/claude-code/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (line 3) and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (top-level line 8 + plugins[0].version line 14) actually blocks `/plugin marketplace update` from refreshing changed plugin files in the user's Claude Code version. Plugin files changed since the pin was set (`skills/planner/SKILL.md` 5 commits, `hooks/hooks.json` 2 commits) but the version was never bumped — `git log` shows the version line only written once in the initial F001 commit. Per Anthropic issue anthropics/claude-code#79950, an unchanged pinned version makes the update command report "already at the latest version" and skip the plugin cache refresh, even though real content changed.

Verification approach: (a) compare the currently installed plugin cache at `~/.claude/plugins/cache/.../agent-plan/<version>/skills/planner/SKILL.md` (and hooks) against the `main` branch to detect staleness; and/or (b) bump the version once and run `/plugin marketplace update` to confirm a refresh occurs. Also confirm the running MCP server version is independent of this pin (it is controlled by the global `agent-plan` CLI via `npx agent-plan mcp` or the plugin's `npx -y @agent-plan/mcp`, not by the plugin `version` field).

Outcome: a definitive yes/no on whether the pin is currently harming plugin-file delivery, plus the user's Claude Code version for reference.
